scopeReview: PSO-1.C–D: local, national, regional and global scales, variations and interpretations revealed by different scales. Applied weighting, aggregation and median comparisons operationalize these objectives without requiring advanced statistical terminology.
varietyReview: Four interpreted stimuli and seven applications distinguish aggregation, changing zones, units versus extent, cross-scale processes, suitable local evidence, comparable boundaries and spatial versus temporal detail. Difficulty and all four keys are varied.
repetitionReview: Reviewed earlier sets: national/local concealment is assessed through new denominators and boundary comparisons rather than a repeat of dot identification or clinic choice. Two aggregation stimuli distinguish rescaling populations from redrawing memberships; separate models corroborate both.

questions.correctOption: Substantial internal variation, with higher rates in the north than in the south.
questions.independentReview: Recomputed the national rate as(90+70+10+30)/4=50 under equal household counts, and northern mean80 versus southern20. The aggregate is consistent, not evidence of uniformly50% local access.

questions.correctOption: 82%, because 820 of the region’s 1,000 residents have the service
questions.independentReview: Independently summed numerator810+10=820 and denominator900+100=1000. Checked unweighted national mean50% differs from the resident-weighted82%; the prompt explicitly asks the latter.

questions.correctOption: Changing aggregation boundaries can change the visible pattern without changing the underlying local observations.
questions.independentReview: Independently reconstructed planI means(A80+B80)/2=80 and(C20+D20)/2=20; planII(A80+C20)/2=50 and(B80+D20)/2=50. Both overall means remain50 with unchanged equal denominators.

questions.correctOption: Country A has the lower national median, while its listed city has the higher city median.
questions.independentReview: Checked national600<800 but city1200>1000. Medians cannot be added or averaged here; no unsupported population weighting or individual rent claim is used.

questions.correctOption: Global, because the investigation follows connections across multiple world regions
questions.independentReview: Matched the explicit multi-continent extent to the global option; the distractors confuse the location of individual observations with the coverage of the investigation.

questions.correctOption: The study groups connected places using a watershed rather than national borders.
questions.independentReview: Compared the bounded three-country basin with single-country and whole-world extents. The criterion is an explicit watershed connection; no claim that all regions must be watersheds is made.

questions.correctOption: Its geographic extent is global, while its observation units remain local.
questions.independentReview: Held the neighborhood unit fixed while varying display extent. Distinguished global coverage of the map from complete sampling coverage, preventing a second unsupported inference.

questions.correctOption: Street-level paths, traffic and crossing conditions around the school
questions.independentReview: Checked the evidence required to compare actual crossing sites: nearby paths and traffic. None of the aggregate alternatives retains site position or conditions.

questions.correctOption: Processes operating at several scales can contribute to a local outcome.
questions.independentReview: Separated outcome scale from candidate mechanism scale. The correct answer permits cross-scale analysis but does not assert a causal estimate unsupported by the prompt.

questions.correctOption: Use compatible geographic units or reconstruct comparable boundaries
questions.independentReview: Tested a counterexample in which population stays put while a district gains a neighborhood through redrawing. Its count changes without migration, demonstrating the need for comparable geographic support.

questions.correctOption: The time interval is finer, but the reported spatial unit remains the country.
questions.independentReview: Varied only the reporting interval and held country aggregation fixed. The supported comparison is temporal refinement without a finer spatial unit.
